title: Medusa and Perseus
subtitle: The look that petrifies
subject: mythologie
description: Medusa petrifies with a look. Perseus defeats her using a mirror shield, then saves Andromeda. The head of the Gorgon becomes a protective symbol.

hero.hook: A look that changes life to stone. A hero who only dares to look at the reflection.

blocks.text: The myth of **Perseus** and **Medusa** is one of the great Greek adventures. It's not just a fight against a monster. It is also the story of beauty transformed into horror, and of a hero who wins through cunning.
Medusa, a [[Gorgon]], petrifies anyone who meets her gaze. Perseus, to survive, agrees to see danger only through a mirror.

According to Ovid's , Medusa is first of all not a monster. She is a young woman with bright hair, priestess in the temple of **Athena**, goddess of wisdom. Her beauty attracts **Poseidon**, god of the seas, who rapes her in the sanctuary. [[Metamorphoses]]

In ancient tragic logic, Athena punishes the victim. Medusa's hair becomes snakes. His look **petrified**. Banished to the ends of the world with her sisters Stheno and Euryale, she lives in a cave surrounded by statues: the unfortunate people who saw her.

blocks.caption: Medusa, Gorgon with a deadly gaze.

blocks.text: The blood from Medusa's left side was deadly poison. The one on the right side could resurrect the dead: a secret that Athena later entrusted to **Asclepius**, god of medicine.

sections.title: Perseus arms himself against the impossible

blocks.text: King **Polydectès** wants to take Perseus away to seduce his mother **Danaé**. He imposes a suicidal challenge on her: bring back the head of Medusa. Perseus is the son of **Zeus**. The gods help him.

**Hermès** gives him winged sandals and a [[Harpe]], an ultra-sharp curved sword. **Hadès** lends him the [[Kunee]], invisibility helmet. Athena offers the decisive advice: her polished bronze shield, to use as a **mirror**.

blocks.caption: Perseus approaches Medusa looking only at his reflection.

blocks.text: Perseus surprises Medusa sleeping. Guided by the reflection, he cuts off his head. From the neckline spring  and the giant . Medusa was still pregnant with Poseidon. [[Pegasus, born of the blood of Medusa]] [[Chrysaor]]

The head retains its power. Perseus puts it in the [[Kibisis]], a magical bag. While flying over Ethiopia, he sees Princess **Andromeda** chained to a rock. It is offered to **Ketos**, sea monster sent by Poseidon to punish the pride of his mother Cassiopeia.

blocks.caption: Perseus frees Andromeda using Medusa's head.

blocks.text: Some legends say that Perseus created red coral by placing Medusa's head on algae: the blood would have hardened the plants.
Perseus petrifies the monster, marries Andromeda, then returns to Seriphos. Facing Polydectes and his court, he sticks his head out. His enemies become statues. The tyranny stops.

Perseus hands over his head to Athena. She fixes it on her **egid**, her divine shield. Medusa goes from being a monster to be slain to a protective power. This effigy, the [[The Gorgoneion]], adorns Greek temples, coins and shields.

Its function is : to deflect evil through the very horror of the face. Over the centuries, Medusa also became a tragic figure, then a modern icon: trauma, power, fascination. Even the house of Versace chose its head to “petrify” the look. [[Apotropaic]]
**Perseus** defeats **Medusa** thanks to the reflection of a shield. The head, given to **Athena**, becomes the **Gorgoneion**, protective symbol of ancient Greece.
